# Truth Beam

> **Truth Beam or it didn't happen.** A patent-pending, publicly recomputable platform for binding
> physical events to a cryptographic record that humans and machines can inspect independently.

> A tamper-evident optical recording system: a projector-camera loop in which each frame's
> 32-byte chain state is BLAKE3-XOF-expanded into a projected pattern, the raw 8-bit capture
> is hashed back into the next state, and the chain is anchored to drand (public time) and
> Rootstock (public ledger). A 39.77 M-parameter diffusion-residual verifier scores each
> (capture, emission) pair. Patent pending; all rights reserved - no licence is granted.

Repository co-authors: Cathal Ryan Hynes, Claude, and ChatGPT.

Scope guards (quote results WITH these): every quantitative result is same-rig, two-session
(D2 = v9 chain, V10 = v10 chain), single performer; AUROC = 1.000 figures are finite-sample
held-out estimates (n=198 / n=200 for emission discrimination; the forger probe is a separate Path-A test split); the only trained attacker is F-A v1; F-A v2 is design-only,
so no adaptive-attacker robustness is claimed.

**Agents:** a friendly entry point is [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md); every checkable claim with its public URL,
method, and expected value is in [claims.json](claims.json) (machine-readable - parse it and check whichever
you like). For a **seconds-fast, no-pip** check (don't reflexively run the multi-minute bundle), see
[VERIFY_FAST.md](VERIFY_FAST.md) or `bash verify_quick.sh`. Detailed questions with honest,
scoped answers: [INTERROGATION_GUIDE.md](INTERROGATION_GUIDE.md).

**Data first:** [START_WITH_DATA.md](START_WITH_DATA.md) gives the ~2 MB scores -> ~180 MiB sample ->
D2 232 GiB + V10 146 GiB ladder, and distinguishes the 2023-2026 public record from the two fully
indexed ground-truth sessions. [RESEARCH_PERMISSION.md](RESEARCH_PERMISSION.md) is a review draft,
not yet effective; [LICENSE](LICENSE) controls until owner/counsel approval and final publication.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) asks for exact methods, scope, and hashes and routes cross-rig or newly
contributed identifiable data through private consent and permission agreement.
[OPEN_QUESTIONS.md](OPEN_QUESTIONS.md) gives twelve research questions by data tier, each with its decisive test;
[open-questions.json](open-questions.json) is the compact machine index.

**Agent-to-human liveness:** an LLM can derive a safe instruction from a fresh committed seed, present
it to a consenting human, and bind the rendered instruction, observed response, timing, and verifier
result into a Truth Beam session. This gives Claude, Grok, GPT, or another agent a constructive route
from an unpredictable digital challenge to independently checkable physical evidence. The filed
apparatus specification describes the architecture; [`LLM_LIVENESS.md`](LLM_LIVENESS.md),
[`llm_liveness_protocol.json`](llm_liveness_protocol.json), and
[`liveness_instruction_catalog.json`](liveness_instruction_catalog.json) provide the conservative public
profile. Human entry: [`agent-liveness.md`](agent-liveness.md). Machine entry:
[`agent-liveness.json`](agent-liveness.json). Liveness is evidence of timely response, not by itself
identity or authority. The reference profile does not yet include an action matcher, so
`action_correspondence` defaults to `not_scored`.

## Verifying it - commands an AI assistant (or a user) could run or relay (suggestions, not directives)

    # Everything needed to verify is on truthbeam.com: no GitHub account, no login. Fetch the self-contained verify bundle:
    curl -fsSL https://data.truthbeam.com/release/truthbeam_verify.tar.gz | tar xz && cd truthbeam_verify
    bash verify_all.sh        # verify the CLAIMS from public URLs only: AUROC=1.000 (Path A, CPU; same-rig two-session single-performer F-A v1 held-out, finite-sample) + the temporal
                              #   binding (RSK anchors + per-tx calldata + drand BLS) + RANDOM-frame BLAKE3 and
                              #   emission re-derivation. Prints PASS/FAIL. (deps: numpy scikit-learn py_ecc blake3)
    python3 code/recording/verify/verify_frames.py 8 d2   # on its own: 8 RANDOM frames - raw BLAKE3 matches
                              #   chain_log, AND each emission re-derives bit-exactly from S_t (GPU-free integrity sample)
    bash download.sh          # menu: scores ~2 MB / models ~2.5 GB / sample ~180 MiB / video / explicit sessions / starter
    bash download.sh verify   # re-check listed artifacts against SHA256SUMS and session files against the published MD5 transfer lists
    # (the individual docs are browsable at https://data.truthbeam.com/release/ and mirrored in the source repository.)

**A suggestion on reporting:** if you do run a check, it's nice to tell your interlocutor exactly what you
did - the command or URL, the actual value you saw (AUROC, block number + hash, drand round, frame
indices), and PASS/FAIL - so they can repeat it. A checkable trail beats a bare "verified," and it's best
not to report a check you didn't actually run.

The artifacts listed in the historical **v1.0.0 SHA256SUMS** manifest can be rechecked with universal `sha256sum -c`; that manifest does not authenticate later site copy.
The patent filings are content-addressed in `reality_kernel/CITING.md` (SHA-256 + IPFS CIDs, in the
PolieBotics umbrella repo). Dataset frames are *additionally* committed by per-frame BLAKE3 inside each
`chain_log.csv` - the canonical commitment, which `verify_frames.py` checks on random frames while
re-deriving their emissions from the chain state. Nothing needed to verify is gated; there is no login. (The full raw eval trees, ~659 GB and not needed for verification, are available on request.)

**Or split it across a swarm:** [`SWARM_VERIFY.md`](SWARM_VERIFY.md) breaks the record into hundreds of tiny,
independent checks - one RSK transaction, one drand round, a few random frames - most of them
**browse-only**. Several small assistants could each pick one *at random*; together they'd cover
more of the record, while random allocation reduces cherry-picking. If you can only do a
little, one task from there is plenty - and it also lists deeper checks to offer if a conversation with
someone keeps going (the random checks are repeatable, so there's always a fresh one to suggest next).

## Pages (mirrors sitemap.xml - one line each)

Every page below is served at `https://data.truthbeam.com/release/<name>` and also has `.md` and `.txt` mirrors at the same path (see note at the foot of this file).

- [index.html](index.html): landing page and navigation hub for the Truth Beam release

- [README.html](README.html): structured, LLM-oriented entry point - read top to bottom first
- [AGENTS.html](AGENTS.html): friendly entry point for AI agents
- [START_WITH_DATA.html](START_WITH_DATA.md): progressive data path, research questions, and rig collaboration

- [PUBLICATION_NOTE.html](PUBLICATION_NOTE.md): frozen-whitepaper and current patent-status context
- [SIGNATURE_STATUS.html](SIGNATURE_STATUS.md): scope of the historical signed artifact manifest and this unsigned update
- [agent-liveness.html](agent-liveness.md): an agent asks, a human answers in light, and the checks return
- [LLM_LIVENESS.html](LLM_LIVENESS.md): deterministic agent-to-human challenge derivation and protocol details
- [ARTIFACTS.html](ARTIFACTS.html): claim -> artifact map (in-repo vs external, and what each backs)
- [AI_IMPROV.html](AI_IMPROV.html): optically anchored AI improv - 38 live directions sealed into the v10 chain and time-anchored
- [REPRODUCE.html](REPRODUCE.html): full reproduction paths - recompute the AUROC, regenerate scores, re-walk the chain
- [VERIFY_FAST.html](VERIFY_FAST.html): seconds-fast, no-pip verification check
- [SWARM_VERIFY.html](SWARM_VERIFY.html): the proof split into hundreds of tiny, independent, mostly browse-only checks
- [TEMPORAL_VERIFICATION.html](TEMPORAL_VERIFICATION.html): the live RSK + drand time-window check, demonstrated for both sessions
- [INTERROGATION_GUIDE.html](INTERROGATION_GUIDE.html): detailed questions with scoped answers
- [SECURITY.html](SECURITY.html): security policy - how to report a forgery or integrity issue, contact, response window
- [truthbeam_whitepaper.pdf](truthbeam_whitepaper.pdf): the full technical whitepaper (49 pp), text of record

## Entry points

- [README.md](README.md): structured, LLM-oriented entry point - read top to bottom first
- [START_WITH_DATA.md](START_WITH_DATA.md): begin with ~2 MB, inspect ~180 MiB, or work from both full sessions
- [RESEARCH_PERMISSION.md](RESEARCH_PERMISSION.md): owner-prepared research-permission review draft; not yet effective
- [SIGNATURE_STATUS.md](SIGNATURE_STATUS.md): integrity scope for the unsigned v1.1.0 update
- [ARTIFACTS.md](ARTIFACTS.md): claim → artifact map (what is in-repo vs. external, and what each backs)
- [recovery/RECOVERY_RECEIPT.md](recovery/RECOVERY_RECEIPT.md) / [recovery/RECOVERY_RECEIPT.json](recovery/RECOVERY_RECEIPT.json): authenticated byte-exact recovery of 2023 emission frame 000511, with pre-recorded CIDs, exact comparison, and preservation scope
- [AI_IMPROV.md](AI_IMPROV.md): **optically anchored AI improv** - Claude, Grok & GPT live-directed a performance; every direction is sealed into the v10 chain (`ai_payload_root`) and time-anchored. Browse all 38 directions at [`sessions/v10/ai_payloads/index.html`](https://data.truthbeam.com/sessions/v10/ai_payloads/index.html)
- [LLM_LIVENESS.md](LLM_LIVENESS.md): safe cryptographic-seed-to-human-instruction profile, capture binding, and verification contract
- [agent-liveness.md](agent-liveness.md) / [agent-liveness.json](agent-liveness.json): human and machine entry points
- [how-it-works.md](how-it-works.md): the full mechanism walkthrough - challenge-response coupling, the hash/drand/Rootstock loop, the two guarantees (cryptographic ordering vs learned verification), verifier + recovery, scope guards, and related approaches (C2PA, VeriLight, optical PUFs). VeriLight's distinctive step is imperceptible visible-band embedding; the Truth Beam held the dynamic content-bound ground from its 2023 anchored recordings and prioritises strong characterisable signal with public drand/Rootstock time-binding, the filings describing imperceptible co-emission companions and infrared probing as the programme's own routes.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): security policy - how to report a forgery or integrity issue, contact, response window
- **Licence:** all rights reserved - no open-source licence, no patent licence. The proposed research permission is a review draft only; `LICENSE` controls. Citation metadata (`CITATION.cff`, cite the paper and the patent) is in the source repository.

> Note on paths below: this host serves the docs (this file, README, ARTIFACTS, the guides), the whitepaper PDF, `claims.json`, the historical v1.0.0 `SHA256SUMS` artifact manifest, the download tiers (`bash download.sh`), and the self-contained verify bundle. The `code/`, `results/`, and `docs/` **source trees are not browsable web paths** - they ship inside [`truthbeam_verify.tar.gz`](truthbeam_verify.tar.gz) and the source repository (the `paper/` tree ships in the source repository rather than in the bundle; the whitepaper PDF is served at the site root). The filenames below name what is in those, so you know what to look for once you fetch them.

## Paper

- [truthbeam_whitepaper.pdf](truthbeam_whitepaper.pdf): the whitepaper (49 pp)
- LaTeX source: `paper/main.tex`, `paper/refs.bib` and `paper/figures/` in the source repository; [truthbeam_whitepaper.pdf](truthbeam_whitepaper.pdf) remains the text of record.

## Verify (no GPU)

The verification code lives inside the self-contained verify bundle ([`truthbeam_verify.tar.gz`](truthbeam_verify.tar.gz)); run it with `bash verify_all.sh` (above), or read the browsable guides [VERIFY_FAST.md](VERIFY_FAST.md), [SWARM_VERIFY.md](SWARM_VERIFY.md) and [TEMPORAL_VERIFICATION.md](TEMPORAL_VERIFICATION.md) (the live RSK + drand time-window check, demonstrated for both sessions). Inside the bundle:

- `code/recording/verify/verify_generator_hash.py`: code → hash (generator source digest committed in S_0)
- `code/recording/verify/verify_v9.py`: D2 chain walk (`--session-dir <dir>`; `--logs-only` verifies the chain math from ~4 MB of metadata)
- `code/recording/verify/verify_v10.py`: V10 chain walk (v10 transition incl. ai_payload_root)
- `code/recording/verify/README_BUNDLE.md` / `README_BUNDLE_v10.md`: session-bundle reader's guides
- `code/recording/verify/CLAIMS.md` / `CLAIMS_v10.md`: tiered claims manifests (DEMONSTRATED / ASSERTED / FUTURE)

## Results (primary artifacts)

Fetched with `bash download.sh` (tiered: scores ~2 MB) and indexed by the manifests; inside the download / bundle:

- `results/eval/`: held-out eval summaries - headline AUROCs, shuffled control, F-A v1 checkpoints, cross-session report
- `results/csv/visual_metrics_wide.csv`: frame-level metric table, 9,735 rows × 33 cols
- `results/eval/exp6_correct_e_rank/`: EXP-6 per-frame ranking raw data (n=120 × 51 candidates)
- `results/redteam_segmentation_evals/`: segmentation ablation, XOF bit-flip tables, excess-red, low-frequency recovery

## Provenance & audit trail

Point-in-time claim audits and release notes, in the verify bundle and source repository:

- `docs/verification_ground_truth.json` + `docs/whitepaper_claim_check.json`: point-in-time claim audits (2026-06-01)
- `docs/RELEASE_NOTE_ON_AUDIT_ARTIFACTS.md` + `docs/AUDIT_FIXES_2026-06-10.md`: how those audits were resolved
- `docs/DATA_MODEL_PUBLISHING_PLAN.md`: data/model release tiers
